slides.title: Constructive Feedback
slides.content:
1. The Sandwich Technique

To give criticism without demotivating someone, use this structure:

1. The Bun (Positive): Start with praise.
"I really appreciate your creativity..."

2. The Meat (Constructive): The area to improve.
"...however, your reports are often late..."

3. The Bun (Positive): End on a high note.
"...but keep up the great design work."

2. Softening Language

Direct criticism can sound rude. Use "softeners":

  • Instead of "You are lazy", say: "You tend to be a bit slow sometimes."
  • Instead of "This is wrong", say: "This could be better."
slides.speech_text: Giving feedback is an art. Never be too direct with negative news. Use the Sandwich Technique: start with a compliment, mention the problem gently using softeners like 'a bit' or 'tend to', and finish with encouragement.

slides.title: The Annual Review
slides.content: Listen to a manager giving a performance review to an employee.
slides.audio_script:
Manager: Hi Tom, thanks for coming in. First, I want to say that your sales numbers this quarter were fantastic. You are very proactive.
        Tom: Thank you, I worked hard on that.
        Manager: However, I have noticed that you tend to be late for the Monday meetings. Punctuality is important for the team morale.
        Tom: I understand. I will work on that.
        Manager: Great. Overall, you are a valuable asset to the team. Let's keep pushing.

quiz.question: What is the positive feedback (The Top Bun)?
What is the area for improvement (The Meat)?

slides.title: Soften the Blow
slides.instruction: Transform rude sentences into professional feedback.

options: Your report seems a bit disorganized.
questions.explanation: Usamos 'seems a bit' para suavizar adjetivos negativos como 'messy' o 'disorganized'.

options: You tend to dominate the conversation.
questions.explanation: 'Tend to' indica un hábito sin acusar directamente a la persona de ser así siempre.

questions.text: Choose the positive adjective for someone who works hard:
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' es un adjetivo formal excelente para 'hard-working'.

slides.title: Roleplay: Give Feedback
slides.system_prompt:
You are an employee named Alex.
        The user is your Manager giving you a performance review.
        
        Scenario:
        1. You (Alex) ask: "How am I doing in the company?"
        2. The user must use the SANDWICH METHOD:
           - Praise your coding skills.
           - Criticize your lack of communication (gently).
           - End with encouragement.
        3. If the user is too rude (e.g., "You are bad at talking"), act hurt/defensive.
        4. If they are polite, accept the feedback gratefully.
slides.initial_message: Hi boss. Do you have a moment? I wanted to ask for some feedback on my recent performance.
slides.user_goal: Give feedback using the Sandwich Method (Positive -> Negative -> Positive).
